learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical principles underlying the operation of the main semiconductor devices: p-n junction diodes, bipolar transistors and field-effect transistors.

Familiarize with the most common analogue electronic circuits, including those built using operational amplifiers (e.g. filters, summing amplifiers, integrators, differentiators), transistors (single-stage and multi-stage amplifiers) and diodes (rectifiers, limiters, non-linear transfer function circuits).
Analyze simple circuits using operational amplifiers, diodes, bipolar transistors and field-effect transistors.
Determine the operating point of an amplifier and calculate its fundamental parameters for small-signal, centre-band conditions, including voltage gain, current gain, input and output resistances.
Plot the frequency response (Bode plots) of linear circuits.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental electronic device physics: diodes and transistors (bipolar and field effect ones)
Single transistor amplifiers: bias networks and small signal analysis
Operational amplifiers: inverting and non-inverting configurations
Non ideal characteristics of the operational amplifiers: input and output impedances, offset voltage, offset and bias currents, slew-rate limitations, limited bandwidth
Application examples of the operational amplifiers
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)
assessment_rules: The examination consists of two distinct stages: a written paper and an oral examination. Admission to the oral examination is conditional upon passing the written paper. The written paper assesses fundamental skills in circuit analysis and semiconductor device physics. The oral examination assesses the ability to present topics, solve analytical/design problems, and discuss theoretical concepts, exercises, or circuits.
